To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) frequency dependence measurements of the fused-silica standards are more accurate than previously reported and (2) the frequency dependence of fused silica is not a constant, but varies significantly from standard to standard.
the frequency dependence of fused silica can be as large as 0.8/spl mu/F/F, and that the relative uncertainty of the frequency dependence can be as low as 0.07/spl mu/F.
the frequency dependence of fused silica is significantly larger than previously reported and is dominated by dielectric relaxation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of the frequency dependence of fused silica, which is a key parameter for the realization of capacitance standards in the low-frequency range.
developing a measurement method for determining the frequency dependence of capacitance standards.
improving the measurement capability of fused-silicas for capacitance standards at frequencies below 1 kHz.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the frequency dependence of fused silica is a function of the specific fused-silica sample, the frequency range of the measurement, the capacitance value of the fused-silica capacitor, and the measurement method.

frequency dependence measurements of the NIST 1-pF standard capacitor have been improved by a factor of three, with the relative combined standard uncertainty now 0.07/spl mu/F/F at the lowest frequency.
the frequency dependence of fused silica is a significant source of measurement uncertainty for capacitance standards.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fused-silica is not a good material for capacitance standards over the frequency range of 200 to 1000 Hz.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of using a 1 pF cross-capacitance as the reference for the measurement of fused-silicas from 200 to2000 Hz.
fused-silica standards with a capacitance of 1 pF and a relative frequency dependence of 0.5 /spl mu/F/Hz can be produced with an uncertainty of about 0.07 % at 200 Hz.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the frequency dependence of fused silica should be measured and reported with the same care as the capacitance itself, and that the uncertainty of the frequency dependence measurement should be reported as well.
the frequency dependence of fused silica can be significant, especially for capacitance standards with capacitances of 10 pF or larger.
the frequency dependence of fused silica can be significantly reduced by selecting a standard with a small change in capacitance with frequency.
